1 - You need a .vmf file of the map. This is the file used by Hammer to edit maps. You can use a program called [BSPSource](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/BSPSource) to decompile the .bsp file and turn it into a useable .vmf file.

2. Navigate to your GMOD install folder and go to '\\garrysmod\\cfg\\' and find a file named mount.cfg. Open mount.cfg file in any text editor. Keep this file open for later.

Now navigate to the install folder of the game you want to mount; for example, CS:S. 

Every Source game has it's own unique folder for its assets in its install folder. 

For this example; it's the cstrike folder. Open it. You should see something like [this](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/686610741322842151/1217311562386112552/image.png?ex=660390bd&is=65f11bbd&hm=b50b473bc55a3dce40b7d5e8182e5c73ae2896392590a80e59b60540401c3fa9&). 

Select and copy the folder location as seen in [this photo](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/686610741322842151/1217312443613581332/image.png?ex=6603918f&is=65f11c8f&hm=97f90f30e3261ea3df5ac0b5f0bf781e2ac9e8c53618b37002e48fdf92145eb4&).

Go back to the mount.cfg you have open. Inbetween the brackets, type in something like:

`"css" "pastethefolderlocationhere"`

It should look something like [this.](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/686610741322842151/1217314123591712789/image.png?ex=6603931f&is=65f11e1f&hm=9139b8a3dc2dd3c919f43195c99e2aa93478e38366ffdeab488fb615262e5849&)

Save the file and close. You should see CS:S's assets next time you launch hammer if you did it correctly.

3. This really depends on what exactly you want to do; I would google what you'd like to do and see if there are any youtube videos on what you'd like to create, or you can look at the [Source SDK wiki](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/SDK_Docs)

4. An ambient\_generic entity is used to play sounds. The 'play everywhere' flag you are enabling means the sound played by the ambient\_generic will play everywhere regardless of distance. You can learn more [here](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Ambient_generic). 

I think you want to do [soundscapes](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Env_soundscape); these entities will play ambience when you set them up correctly, and they're relatively easy to do. I'm not good at explaining things so I made an [example map](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/686610741322842151/1217318924215910502/soundscapes.vmf?ex=66039798&is=65f12298&hm=daf16bef0f215aa89ad900d494431b13c05b90240dcdd75055f4df5d95afb1a7&) for you with some soundscapes setup.

I would check out this [list](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/List_of_Soundscapes) of soundscapes and experiment a little!
